files.import_probe_method: direct `importlib.import_module('tac.witness_dsl.taskspace_counted_xip2_chronological_a3')` -> rc=0, IMPORT_OK, 25 __all__ exports; corroborated by pytest collection of its test file

findings.what: `_realize_y0` uses a bare `assert parsed.transport is not None` to narrow the type before reading `parsed.transport.xi` at :819. Under `python -O` the assert is stripped, so a None transport would raise AttributeError instead of the module's typed CountedXIP2ChronologicalA3Error. The condition cannot currently be reached (ParsedCountedXIP2ChronologicalA3PacketV1.__post_init__ :339-341 already refuses a XIP2_WARP packet with transport=None), so this is a contract gap, not a live bug.
findings.fix: Replace with `if parsed.transport is None: raise CountedXIP2ChronologicalA3Error("active packet omitted exact XIP2 transport")` so the fail-closed typed-error contract holds under -O.

findings.what: `decode_counted_xip2_chronological_a3_packet` always calls `_decode_once` twice and compares, with no opt-out. For XIP2_WARP_V1 that doubles a per-pair ground-homography warp (plus a resize in SCORER_THEN_FACTOR2), and every G16 search neighbour goes through `compile_...` -> `decode_...`. This is a real constant-factor cost on the search hot path (the 19-test inverse-solver file spends 20.7s largely here). The double decode is deliberate and is asserted by tests, so it should stay the default.
findings.fix: Keep double-decode as the default but expose an explicit parameter (e.g. `verify_determinism: bool = True`) so a bounded inner search loop can verify once per arm instead of once per candidate.

findings.what: `_resize_operator()` is `@lru_cache(maxsize=1)` and hands the same DisjointResizeOperator instance to every decode with no defensive copy. Correct today because the operator is used read-only (`apply` / `realize_factor2_uint8`), but any future mutating method on that class would cross-contaminate independent decodes through the shared cache and defeat the deterministic-double-decode check, which would also see the same mutated object twice.
findings.fix: Document the read-only requirement on the cached accessor, or have DisjointResizeOperator expose immutability (frozen dataclass / read-only arrays) so the sharing is enforced rather than assumed.

findings.what: SUBSTITUTED-ARCHIVE SOUNDNESS HOLE (MEASURED). `build_bridge_receipt` accepts an optional `scored_archive` and, at :323-327, validates it only with `_require_file_row` - which checks that the caller's declared path/bytes/sha256 match the file on disk. Nothing binds that file to the G22 witness. The rate term is then priced on those bytes (:327 `archive_bytes = int(scored_archive_row["bytes"])`) while d_seg/d_pose are inherited from the G22 object, and the verdict at :344-348 still reads MEASURED_FULL_N600_SAME_OBJECT_BRIDGE_INSIDE_ADVISORY_TARGET with `scored_output_matches_g22_reference: True` hardcoded at :358. I reproduced this: passing an unrelated 11-byte file (b'X'*11, no relation to the 16-byte G22 selected archive) produced verdict=MEASURED_FULL_N600_SAME_OBJECT_BRIDGE_INSIDE_ADVISORY_TARGET, priced_bytes=11, score=0.030007324448484342, inside_target_sublevel=True. The one honest signal, `scored_archive_matches_g22_selected: False` (:356), is recorded in artifact_identity but is never consulted by the verdict or by the score row. The module docstring claims the row is 'a scorer row measured on *that exact object*'; on this path it is not. Blast radius is bounded because the receipt is stamped research_only/score_claim False/promotion_eligible False/pointer_moved False, so it cannot move the pointer - but it can emit a plausible 'inside advisory target' row for an archive that was never scored.
findings.fix: ROOT CAUSE: the membership check is currently IMPOSSIBLE to write, because `validate_terminal_g22` only reads `archive_artifact.selected` (:135-136) and never captures the identity of the SOURCE spelling, even though the G22 receipt's whole point is that source and selected decode identically (it asserts `source_raw_sha256 == selected_raw_sha256` at :170-171). So `build_bridge_receipt` has no proven-equivalent set to test membership against. Two-part fix: (1) extend `validate_terminal_g22` to also capture `archive_artifact.source`'s file row when present, and return the set of proven-equivalent archive identities; (2) in `build_bridge_receipt`, require `scored_archive_row` to be a member of that set - `if scored_archive_row not in g22_closure['equivalent_archives']: raise TaskspaceBridgeEvalError('scored archive is not a G22-proven-equivalent spelling')`. Interim one-liner if (1) is deferred: refuse any `scored_archive` that differs from the G22 selected archive, or downgrade the verdict token to `..._SUBSTITUTED_RATE_ARCHIVE_...` and set `scored_output_matches_g22_reference` to False.

findings.what: Thin coverage: 4 tests for 407 lines. Untested refusal branches include the scorer-row gates at :314-320 (pair_count != 600, device != 'cpu', deterministic_algorithms not True, raw_sha256 differing from the G22 witness), `file_identity`'s symlink/non-regular-file refusal at :86, and the cached-vs-recomputed pointer disagreement at :234-235. Those are the fail-closed paths that carry the module's authority claims, so they are exactly the ones worth pinning.
findings.fix: Add one parametrized test per scorer-row gate and one for the pointer cached/derived mismatch; they are cheap (pure dict inputs, no file I/O except the symlink case).

findings.what: `_parse_xip2_exact` reaches into another module's private API: `xi_pose_coder._channel_delta_decode(payload, offset, pair_count)`. The symbol exists (src/tac/boundary_math/xi_pose_coder.py:217) so this works today, but it is an attribute access on an imported module rather than a `from ... import`, so a rename or removal upstream produces no import-time signal - it fails at first SE3_XI decode, which is a counted-transport path.
findings.fix: Either promote `_channel_delta_decode` to a public name in xi_pose_coder, or import it explicitly (`from tac.boundary_math.xi_pose_coder import _channel_delta_decode`) so a rename breaks at import rather than at decode.

findings.what: `_parse_xip2_exact` re-implements the per-coder XIP2 body dispatch (coder ids 0-3, :196-216) that `xi_pose_coder.parse_xi_payload` already implements, then cross-checks the two decoders agree (:224-228). The duplication is deliberate defence-in-depth and the docstring says so ('Use the canonical XIP2 decoders while independently enforcing EOF'), but it means a new coder id must be added in two places; add it only upstream and SE3_XI transport silently refuses every payload using it with 'unknown XIP2 coder id'.
findings.fix: No code change required - add a comment at :215 pointing at xi_pose_coder's coder table so the two-place edit is discoverable, or derive the accepted id set from a shared constant in xi_pose_coder.

files.import_probe_method: direct `importlib.import_module('tac.witness_dsl.taskspace_quantized_xip2_inverse_solver')` -> rc=0, IMPORT_OK, 20 __all__ exports; corroborated by pytest collection of its test file

findings.what: NO-FAKE #6 CHECK (search-masquerading-as-solver): I checked this hard, and the mechanism IS a search, not a solve. `run_quantized_xip2_inverse_search` (:1803) does bounded coordinate descent over the int16 XIP2 lattice: for each arm it walks a seeded coordinate order (:1961), proposes +/- step neighbours bounded by q_level (:1972-1977), evaluates each through the real G13 receiver plus an external scoring callback, and takes the argmin by (complete_score, packet_sha256) (:2024). There is no closed-form, variational, KKT, or preimage solve anywhere in the file. HOWEVER, NO-FAKE #6's escape conditions (a) honest labelling and (b) documented real mechanism are both substantially MET inside the module: the docstring calls it 'an encoder-side, research-only bounded search' (:4-5); FORMULATION_SCOPE is literally 'FIXED_SCALE_DIRECT_INT16_COORDINATE_SEARCH_V1' (:58); every public class and the entry point are named ...Search...; the receipt carries `direct_quantized_receiver_search: True` and `affine_xi_pose_model_used: False` (:803-804); and the docstring explicitly disclaims an analytic path ('no affine pose model, Jacobian surrogate, dense target, scorer, or archive builder lives here'). The ONLY misleading surface left is the filename `..._inverse_solver.py` (inherited from .omx/research/original_taskspace_inverse_witness_codec_20260725/SPEC_g16_quantized_xip2_inverse_solver_20260726.md) and the error class name QuantizedXIP2InverseError. A future grep for 'solver' lands here and reads as a solve. Rename is cheap: the only code importer is its own test file.
findings.fix: Rename the module to `taskspace_quantized_xip2_inverse_search.py` (only importer is src/tac/witness_dsl/tests/test_taskspace_quantized_xip2_inverse_solver.py), or - if the SPEC filename must be preserved for lineage - add one docstring line: 'FILENAME NOTE: "solver" is historical from SPEC_g16; the mechanism is a bounded coordinate SEARCH over the int16 lattice, not a closed-form solve.'

findings.what: SELF-POISONING RESUME (fail-closed, deliberate, but undocumented recovery). `_atomic_publish` writes `.<name>.tmp`, fsyncs, then hardlinks. A crash in the window between :1085 (fsync) and :1089 (os.link) leaves the temp file behind. On the next resume, `_load_stage_store` :1189-1191 refuses any run-directory entry that does not match `stage-\d{8}-(evaluation|terminal)\.json`, so the whole run directory becomes permanently unresumable with the message 'unexpected temporary/partial/run file: .stage-00000005-evaluation.json.tmp'. This is intentional and is pinned by test_resume_rejects_foreign_config_source_chain_partial_and_duplicate (test file :499-509), and it never corrupts data - but the error text gives the operator no recovery instruction, which conflicts with the repo's resumability-is-P0 discipline.
findings.fix: Keep the refusal, improve the message: include 'delete this temp file to resume; its contents were never chained' in the raise at :1191. Optionally, accept a temp file whose bytes equal the pending payload and re-link it.

findings.what: The only silent-exception site in the module: `_atomic_publish`'s `finally` block swallows both OSError and QuantizedXIP2InverseError with a bare `pass` (:1108-1109) while cleaning up the temp file. It is narrowly scoped to cleanup, is commented, and cannot mask a failed publish (the publish path itself raises), but a leaked temp file here is exactly what triggers the permanent-refusal case above, so the swallow and the refusal compound.
findings.fix: Leave the swallow (raising in `finally` would mask the real error) but record the leaked path - e.g. re-raise nothing and instead let the message in the sister fix above name the file.

files.import_probe_method: direct `importlib.import_module('tac.witness_dsl.taskspace_same_class_realization_encoder')` -> rc=0, IMPORT_OK, 21 __all__ exports; corroborated by pytest collection of its test file

findings.what: SCALABILITY WALL in `acquire_same_class_realization_repair_programs`. The function emits one proposal per (family x prefix_order x prefix_count): with the test plan that is 4 families x 2 orders x 5 prefixes = 40 proposals, and each one runs `_build_program` (:1220, a Python loop over every selected cell) followed by `validate_same_class_realization_program_against_evidence` (:1281, a second Python loop over every expanded cell). Because `prefix_cell_counts` is geometric, the summed cell work is roughly 2x debt_count per (family, order), i.e. O(4 x families x debt_count) Python-level iterations. The rest of the module is properly vectorized, so this is the one hot spot; at n600-scale realization debt it dominates. Encoder-only, so it never runs in the receiver, and the only bound is whatever plan the caller passes.
findings.fix: Vectorize the RLE in `_build_program` (np.diff over the sorted (pair,row,col) address array to find run boundaries) and vectorize `validate_...` (build the expanded address array once and index the debt mask/label arrays in bulk instead of per-cell). Both preserve exact output ordering.

findings.what: `N2_STAGE_ABLATION_PRIORITY_RECEIPT_SHA256` is a hardcoded 64-hex literal that gates evidence admission at :381 and receipt admission at :685. I verified it is NOT an orphan constant: the same digest appears in five .omx/research documents (SPEC_g12_same_class_realization_encoder_20260726.md, SPEC_g10, SPEC_g14, SPEC_g17, and codex_findings_taskspace_semantic_realization_decoupling_20260726_codex.md), so the provenance exists. But the module carries no pointer to any of them, so a reader hitting the gate has no path from the code to the receipt it enforces.
findings.fix: Add a comment at :47 citing `.omx/research/original_taskspace_inverse_witness_codec_20260725/SPEC_g12_same_class_realization_encoder_20260726.md` as the source of the digest, so the value-provenance chain is reachable from the code.
